This module applies the same saved NIST excerpt the last module introduced — no new source was
independently fetched, since the new content here is application (categorizing and selecting
controls for the eQMS), not new citation. The links below were checked at the time this page was
written.

- **[NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2, "Risk Management Framework for Information Systems and
  Organizations"](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.800-37r2.pdf)**
  (PDF, final, December 2018) — the document behind both quotes in this lesson (Categorize's
  purpose statement and Select's one-line action), via the same saved excerpt in `sources/nist/`
  used last module. Curl-checked directly from this session: returns HTTP 200.

- **[Risk management frameworks side by side](../risk-frameworks-side-by-side/index.qmd)** — this
  course's first module: the comparison that justified borrowing RMF's structure for the eQMS in
  the first place, and where the Categorize and Select steps were first named (without being
  applied). Read it for the full three-framework comparison this module assumes.

- **NIST SP 800-53** — the separate publication that actually defines control families and
  numbered controls. Not independently fetched or quoted anywhere in this curriculum; mentioned
  here only so you know where the real catalog lives if Lakeshore ever needs more than the family
  names this module uses.

- **[The 3 Tasks in the CATEGORIZE Step of the NIST RMF](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hNrV2VuLeh8)**
  (Denise Tawwab, from oEmbed `author_name`) — the video embedded in this lesson. A third-party
  RMF training walkthrough of the tasks inside Categorize, aimed at federal practitioners; NIST
  itself does not appear to publish a video on this step. Verified embeddable via YouTube oEmbed
  on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST FIPS 199, "Standards for Security Categorization of Federal Information and Information
  Systems"](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/199/final)** — NIST's catalog page for the standard
  that defines the low/moderate/high impact framing across confidentiality, integrity, and
  availability. Read it if you want the source of the vocabulary behind this lesson's
  "moderate-impact" label; Lakeshore's use is voluntary and borrowed, not a FIPS compliance
  claim. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-60 Vol. 1 Rev. 1, "Guide for Mapping Types of Information and Information Systems
  to Security Categories"](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/60/v1/r1/final)** — NIST's guide to
  working out an impact level from the types of information a system holds, the practical
  companion to Categorize. Read it when you want to see how a federal agency would structure the
  reasoning this lesson does informally for the eQMS. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-53B, "Control Baselines for Information Systems and
  Organizations"](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/b/upd1/final)** — the NIST publication
  that pairs the low, moderate, and high impact levels with starting control baselines, which is
  what the lesson's "initial set of controls" refers to. Not quoted anywhere in this curriculum;
  linked so you know where the real baselines live. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 (with Update 1), "Security and Privacy Controls for Information
  Systems and Organizations"](https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/sp/800/53/r5/upd1/final)** — NIST's
  catalog page for the control catalog itself, with the control families this lesson names as
  concepts. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).

- **[NIST SP 1314, "NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF) Small Enterprise Quick Start
  Guide"](https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/SpecialPublications/NIST.SP.1314.pdf)** — a short,
  plain-language NIST guide written for small organizations that walks the RMF steps, including
  Categorize and Select. The closest thing NIST publishes to an approachable version of this
  lesson; read it before the full SP 800-37. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11
  (HTTP 200).

## Keep learning

Not official sources — good places to learn more about categorizing systems and choosing controls.

- **[Types of Security Controls | CISSP Study Guide](https://destcert.com/resources/types-security-controls/)** (Destination Certification, commercial CISSP trainer) — administrative, technical and physical controls, and preventive, detective and corrective functions, explained the way the exam frames them. Useful vocabulary when you tailor a control set. CISSP Domain 1. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[Security Risk Assessment Methods: Quantitative & Qualitative](https://destcert.com/resources/risk-assessment-methods/)** (Destination Certification, commercial CISSP trainer) — clear comparison of qualitative and quantitative approaches, which helps you reason to an impact level instead of asserting one. CISSP Domain 1. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
- **[CRISC Certification overview](https://www.isaca.org/credentialing/crisc)** (ISACA) — the outline of ISACA's risk-focused certification (risk identification, assessment, response, control monitoring). Even if you never sit the exam, the domain list is a good map of the risk-and-controls skill set. Verified loading via `curl` on 2026-11-11 (HTTP 200).
